subject.title: feat(memory): provenance-gated memory with dreaming on by default

question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed provenance, automatic dreaming, user-model, and standing-intent product direction as a focused program, or require it to be split before review continues?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug fix: it adds durable state, new default background behavior, new memory artifacts, and new agent-facing behavior while the current branch also contains broad unrelated changes.

options.title: Split and sponsor the memory series
options.body: Keep the intended memory work, but separate it from unrelated UI, CI, channel, dependency, protocol, and cleanup changes before approving the product direction.

options.title: Accept the bundle as one coordinated change
options.body: Explicitly own the combined compatibility, security-review, and regression surface and request complete end-to-end upgrade proof before landing.

options.title: Pause the feature direction
options.body: Defer the new default-memory behavior until maintainers decide whether automatic dreaming, USER.md, and standing intents belong in the current product scope.

recommendation.title: Split and sponsor the memory series
recommendation.body: Keep the intended memory work, but separate it from unrelated UI, CI, channel, dependency, protocol, and cleanup changes before approving the product direction.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied branch history shows steipete authored the coordinated memory design and is the clearest available routing candidate for narrowing or explaining its intended product boundary.
